questions.question: An idealized centrifugal pump (blade outer radius of 50 mm) consumes 2 kW power while running at 3000 rpm. The entry of the liquid into the pump is axial and exit from the pump is radial with respect to impeller. If the losses are neglected, then the mass flow rate of the liquid through the pump is ______kg/s (round off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: The theoretical head (Euler's head) is given by [latex] \begin{aligned} \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{e}} &=\frac{\mathrm{u}_{2} \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{w} 2}}{\mathrm{g}} \\ &=\frac{\mathrm{u}_{2}^{2}}{\mathrm{g}} \text { as }\left(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{w} 2}=\mathrm{u}_{2} \text { for radial exit }\right) \end{aligned}[/latex] Thus, [latex] P_{t h}=\rho g Q H_{c}[/latex] [latex] =\rho g Q \times \frac{u_{2}^{2}}{g} [/latex] [latex] =\rho \mathrm{Q} \mathrm{u}_{2}^{2} [/latex] [latex] P_{t h}=\dot{m} u_{2}^{2} [/latex] or, [latex] \dot{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{th}}}{\mathrm{u}_{2}^{2}} [/latex] where, [latex] u_{2}=\frac{\pi \mathrm{d}_{2} \mathrm{N}}{60}=\pi \times 0.1 \times \frac{3000}{60}=5 \pi \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} [/latex] Hence, [latex] \dot{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{2 \times 10^{3}}{(5 \pi)^{2}}=8.11 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
The theoretical head (Euler's head) is given by
[latex] \begin{aligned} \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{e}} &=\frac{\mathrm{u}_{2} \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{w} 2}}{\mathrm{g}} \\ &=\frac{\mathrm{u}_{2}^{2}}{\mathrm{g}} \text { as }\left(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{w} 2}=\mathrm{u}_{2} \text { for radial exit }\right) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Thus,
[latex] P_{t h}=\rho g Q H_{c}[/latex]
[latex] =\rho g Q \times \frac{u_{2}^{2}}{g} [/latex]
[latex] =\rho \mathrm{Q} \mathrm{u}_{2}^{2} [/latex]
[latex] P_{t h}=\dot{m} u_{2}^{2} [/latex]
or,
[latex] \dot{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{th}}}{\mathrm{u}_{2}^{2}} [/latex]
where, [latex] u_{2}=\frac{\pi \mathrm{d}_{2} \mathrm{N}}{60}=\pi \times 0.1 \times \frac{3000}{60}=5 \pi \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} [/latex]
Hence, [latex] \dot{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{2 \times 10^{3}}{(5 \pi)^{2}}=8.11 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}[/latex]

questions.question: An air standard Otto cycle has thermal efficiency of 0.5 and the mean effective pressure of the cycle is 1000 kPa. questions.explanation_html:
Given:

[latex] \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{m}}=100 \mathrm{kPa} [/latex]
[latex] \gamma=1.4 [/latex]
[latex] \mathrm{R}=0.287 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \mathrm{K} [/latex]
[latex] \mathrm{P}_{1}=100 \mathrm{kPa} [/latex]
[latex] \mathrm{T}_{1}=300 \mathrm{K} [/latex]
[latex] \eta_{0}=0.5=1-\frac{1}{(\mathrm{r})^{\gamma-1}} [/latex]
[latex] 0.5=1-\frac{1}{(\mathrm{r})^{1.4-1}} [/latex]
[latex] \mathrm{r}=5.656 [/latex]
At state(1)
[latex] \mathrm{P}_{1} \mathrm{v}_{1}=\mathrm{RT}_{1} [/latex]
[latex] 100 v_{1}=0.287 \times 300 [/latex]
[latex] \mathrm{v}_{1}=0.861 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{kg} [/latex]
[latex] \mathrm{r}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{1}}{\mathrm{v}_{2}} [/latex]
[latex] \mathrm{v}_{2}=0.1522 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{kg} [/latex]
[latex] P_{m}=\frac{W_{\text {net }}}{v_{1}-v_{2}} [/latex]

[latex] \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{net}}=708.77 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}[/latex]

questions.question: A through hole is drilled in an aluminum alloy plate of 15 mm thickness with a drill bit of diameter 10 mm, at a feed of 0.25 mm/rev and a spindle speed of 1200 rpm. If the specific energy required for cutting this material is 0.7 [latex]N\cdot m/mm^3[/latex], the power required for drilling is______W (round off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: Given data [latex] \begin{array}{l} \mathrm{t}=\text { thickness }=15 \mathrm{mm} \\ \mathrm{d}=\operatorname{dia} \text { of drill }=10 \mathrm{mm} \\ \mathrm{f}=0.25 \mathrm{mm} / \mathrm{rev} \\ \text { Speed, } \mathrm{N}=1200 \mathrm{rpm} \\ \text { Specific cutting energy }=0.7 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{mm}^{3} \\ \text { S.P.C.E. }=\frac{\text { Power }}{\mathrm{MRR}} \\ \text { Power }=\mathrm{MRR} \times \mathrm{S.P.C.E} \\ =\text { Area of drill } \times(\mathrm{Feed} / \mathrm{sec}) \times \mathrm{S.P.C.E}\\=\frac{\pi}{4} \mathrm{d}^{2} \times \frac{\mathrm{f}}{60} \times \mathrm{N} \times \mathrm{S.P.C.E} \\ =\frac{\pi}{4} \times 10^{2} \times \frac{0.25}{60} \times 1200 \times 0.7=274.75 \mathrm{W}  \end{array}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given data
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \mathrm{t}=\text { thickness }=15 \mathrm{mm} \\ \mathrm{d}=\operatorname{dia} \text { of drill }=10 \mathrm{mm} \\ \mathrm{f}=0.25 \mathrm{mm} / \mathrm{rev} \\ \text { Speed, } \mathrm{N}=1200 \mathrm{rpm} \\ \text { Specific cutting energy }=0.7 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{mm}^{3} \\ \text { S.P.C.E. }=\frac{\text { Power }}{\mathrm{MRR}} \\ \text { Power }=\mathrm{MRR} \times \mathrm{S.P.C.E} \\ =\text { Area of drill } \times(\mathrm{Feed} / \mathrm{sec}) \times \mathrm{S.P.C.E}\\=\frac{\pi}{4} \mathrm{d}^{2} \times \frac{\mathrm{f}}{60} \times \mathrm{N} \times \mathrm{S.P.C.E} \\ =\frac{\pi}{4} \times 10^{2} \times \frac{0.25}{60} \times 1200 \times 0.7=274.75 \mathrm{W} \end{array}[/latex]

questions.question: In an orthogonal machining with a single point cutting tool of rake angle [latex]10^{\circ}[/latex], the uncut chip thickness and the chip thickness are 0.125mm and 0.22mm,respectively. Using Merchant's first solution for the condition of minimum cutting force, the coefficient of friction at the chip-tool interface is ______ (round off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{array}{l} \alpha=10^{\circ}, t_{l}=0.125, \quad t_{2}=0.22 \\ r=\frac{0.125}{0.22}=0.57 \\ \text { shear angle, } \phi=\tan ^{-1}\left[\frac{r \cos \alpha_{0}}{1-r \sin \alpha_{0}}\right] \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} \phi &=\tan ^{-1}\left[\frac{0.57 \cos 10}{1-0.57 \sin 10}\right] \\ \phi &=31.8 \end{aligned} \end{array}[/latex] From Merchant's [latex]I^{\text {st}}[/latex] solution [latex] \begin{aligned} 2 \phi+\beta-\alpha_{0}=90 & \\ \beta=90+\alpha_{0}-2 \phi &=90+10-2 \times 31.8 \\ &=36.4^{0} \end{aligned}[/latex] Coefficient of friction, [latex] \mu=\tan \beta=\tan 36.4=0.737[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{array}{l} \alpha=10^{\circ}, t_{l}=0.125, \quad t_{2}=0.22 \\ r=\frac{0.125}{0.22}=0.57 \\ \text { shear angle, } \phi=\tan ^{-1}\left[\frac{r \cos \alpha_{0}}{1-r \sin \alpha_{0}}\right] \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} \phi &=\tan ^{-1}\left[\frac{0.57 \cos 10}{1-0.57 \sin 10}\right] \\ \phi &=31.8 \end{aligned} \end{array}[/latex]
From Merchant's [latex]I^{\text {st}}[/latex] solution
[latex] \begin{aligned} 2 \phi+\beta-\alpha_{0}=90 & \\ \beta=90+\alpha_{0}-2 \phi &=90+10-2 \times 31.8 \\ &=36.4^{0} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Coefficient of friction, [latex] \mu=\tan \beta=\tan 36.4=0.737[/latex]

questions.question: The annual demand of valves per year in a company is 10,000 units. The current order quantity is 400 valves per order. The holding cost is Rs. 24 per valve per year and the ordering cost is Rs. 400 per order. If the current order quantity is changed to Economic Order Quantity, then the saving in the total cost of inventory per year will be Rs.______(round off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: Annual demand (D) = 10000 units Holding cost ([latex]C_{c}[/latex]) = 24 /unit / year Ordering cost ([latex]C_{0}[/latex]) = 400 /order Order quantity (Q)=400 units [latex] \begin{aligned} \left.\mathrm{TC}\right|_{\mathrm{Q}=400}-\left.\mathrm{TC}\right|_{\mathrm{EOQ}}&=\left[\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{2} \times \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{C}}+\frac{\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{Q}} \times \mathrm{C}_{0}\right]\\ &-[\sqrt{2 \mathrm{DC}_{0} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{c}}}] \\ &=\left[\frac{400}{2} \times 24+\frac{10000}{400} \times 400\right] \\ &-[\sqrt{2 \times 10000 \times 400 \times 24}] \\ &=(4800+10000)-(13856) \\ &=943.60 \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Annual demand (D) = 10000 units
Holding cost ([latex]C_{c}[/latex]) = 24 /unit / year
Ordering cost ([latex]C_{0}[/latex]) = 400 /order
Order quantity (Q)=400 units
[latex] \begin{aligned} \left.\mathrm{TC}\right|_{\mathrm{Q}=400}-\left.\mathrm{TC}\right|_{\mathrm{EOQ}}&=\left[\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{2} \times \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{C}}+\frac{\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{Q}} \times \mathrm{C}_{0}\right]\\ &-[\sqrt{2 \mathrm{DC}_{0} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{c}}}] \\ &=\left[\frac{400}{2} \times 24+\frac{10000}{400} \times 400\right] \\ &-[\sqrt{2 \times 10000 \times 400 \times 24}] \\ &=(4800+10000)-(13856) \\ &=943.60 \end{aligned}[/latex]
